definition.description: Whether the patient used azithromycin prior to the start of treatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the pretreatment medical record mentions the prescription, administration, or completion of a course of azithromycin.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if there is no mention of azithromycin in the pretreatment record.
definition.name: azithromycin_use

definition.description: The mutation status of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) biomarker.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the reported EGFR mutation status from pretreatment records. Map 'wild type' or 'negative' to 'Wild type' and 'mutant', 'positive', or specific named EGFR mutations to 'Mutant'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent absent or ambiguous documentation as null.
definition.name: biomarker_egfr_status

definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) reported in ml/min from the pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent missing or ambiguous GFR documentation as null.
definition.name: biomarker_fgfr_status

definition.description: The technique or procedure used to obtain the tissue biopsy specimen.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the specific method used to obtain the biopsy specimen (e.g., bronchoscopic, needle biopsy) from the procedure or pathology documentation.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no biopsy method is documented.
definition.name: biopsy_method

definition.description: Whether the patient is currently receiving or has a documented history of bisphosphonate therapy.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is receiving or has received bisphosphonate therapy. This is identified by explicit mentions of 'bisphosphonate' or specific bisphosphonate medications (e.g., zoledronic acid, pamidronate, alendronate) in the medication list or clinical narrative.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if bisphosphonate therapy is not mentioned or is explicitly denied in the record.
definition.name: bisphosphonate_therapy_status

definition.description: The patient's blood pressure, specifically the systolic value.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the blood pressure measurement from the pretreatment record. When blood pressure is recorded as a systolic/diastolic pair (e.g., 128/78 mmHg), extract the systolic (first) value. If only a single numeric value is provided for blood pressure, extract that value.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if blood pressure is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: blood_pressure

definition.description: A measurement of the amount of nitrogen in the blood that comes from the urea produced by the liver, used primarily to assess renal function.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of blood urea nitrogen (BUN) from the comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) or specific renal function laboratory tests.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the value is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: blood_urea_nitrogen

definition.description: The patient's body mass index (BMI), a measure of body fat based on height and weight.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for BMI in kg/m² from the pretreatment record, typically located in the vital signs or physical examination sections.
definition.missing_value_rule: If BMI is not documented and cannot be calculated from height and weight, the value is null.
definition.name: bmi

definition.description: The patient's body temperature at the time of the clinical encounter.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the patient's body temperature from the vital signs section of the clinical record. If the value is recorded in Fahrenheit, convert it to Celsius using the formula: °C = (°F - 32) / 1.8.
definition.missing_value_rule: If body temperature is not documented, explicitly denied (e.g., 'no fever'), or is ambiguous, the value is represented as null.
definition.name: body_temperature

definition.description: The patient's body weight recorded prior to the start of treatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the patient's body weight in kilograms (kg). If the value is reported in pounds (lbs), convert it to kilograms.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if body weight is not documented or cannot be reliably extracted.
definition.name: body_weight

payload.coverage: Cover every supplied candidate, including weak/unevaluable candidates.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.name: theme

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
